// Package anthropic is a minimal stand-in for anthropic-sdk-go: just enough surface for the fixture
// to compile and for the codemod's rewrite to be type-checked by a real compiler.
//
// It is deliberately typed the way the real SDK is, because that is what makes the build gate's test
// meaningful rather than decorative. Two properties are load-bearing, and both mirror the real SDK:
//
//  1. Model is a NAMED STRING TYPE. Rewriting Model to an undefined identifier must FAIL to compile;
//     rewriting it to a string literal must SUCCEED.
//
//  2. A message carries its ROLE IN A FUNCTION (NewUserMessage), never in a bare string field, and its
//     text in a block constructor (NewTextBlock). This is not decoration — it is the property the
//     codemod's refusal boundary rests on. Because the role is a function and the block is a
//     constructor, a single-turn construction contains EXACTLY ONE string expression (the prompt), so
//     "the sole string expression" locates the prompt with zero per-SDK knowledge.
//
//     The `Message{Role string; Content string}` shape this stub used to have would carry TWO bare
//     string literals per message, so every prompt override against it would refuse as ambiguous — a
//     refusal that says nothing about real SDKs, because no real Go SDK is shaped that way. A stub
//     that refuses for a reason reality never produces makes the boundary untestable.
package anthropic

type Model string

const (
	ModelClaudeOpus4_6 Model = "claude-opus-4-6"
	ModelClaudeSonnet4 Model = "claude-sonnet-4"
)

// MessageParamRole is the real SDK's typed role constant — a role is never a bare string literal.
type MessageParamRole string

const (
	MessageParamRoleUser      MessageParamRole = "user"
	MessageParamRoleAssistant MessageParamRole = "assistant"
)

// ContentBlockParam is one block of a message's content. Built by NewTextBlock, not by a literal.
type ContentBlockParam struct {
	Type string
	Text string
}

// NewTextBlock wraps prompt text in a content block. The codemod replaces the ARGUMENT of this call
// and nothing else, which is what makes the rewrite type-preserving: a string expression swapped for
// a string expression type-checks exactly where the original did.
func NewTextBlock(text string) ContentBlockParam {
	return ContentBlockParam{Type: "text", Text: text}
}

// MessageParam is one turn. Its role is set by the constructor below, never spelled at the call site.
type MessageParam struct {
	Role    MessageParamRole
	Content []ContentBlockParam
}

// NewUserMessage carries the role in the FUNCTION — the property the refusal boundary rests on.
func NewUserMessage(blocks ...ContentBlockParam) MessageParam {
	return MessageParam{Role: MessageParamRoleUser, Content: blocks}
}

type MessageNewParams struct {
	Model     Model
	MaxTokens int
	Messages  []MessageParam
}

type Response struct{ Text string }

type messages struct{}

func (messages) New(ctx any, p MessageNewParams) (*Response, error) {
	return &Response{Text: "stub"}, nil
}

type Client struct{ Messages messages }

func NewClient() *Client { return &Client{} }
